nodes.summary: Spring Cloud Config Server that serves centralized `application.properties`/`bootstrap.properties` to every other service at startup; also registers itself as a Eureka client so it can be discovered.
responsibilities: Serve externalized configuration to all other modules over HTTP at boot

testHints: Verify a dependent service's context fails or degrades gracefully when this module is down
openQuestions: Where the backing config repository (git/native) is configured was not inspected

Serve department data to employee-service and report-service over REST
sideEffects: Writes to the departments Mongo collection
Serves inbound REST calls from employee-service and report-service
invariants: departmentId must uniquely resolve to at most one department
failureModes: Being down turns cross-service salary lookups in employee-service/report-service into NPEs or 5xx responses since callers do not null-check the response
testHints: Contract test for GET /api/v1/department/{id} and GET /api/v1/department/salary/{minSalary} response shape

nodes.summary: Netflix Eureka service registry that every other module registers with and discovers peers through; a single point of failure for service-to-service DNS/lookup.
responsibilities: Maintain the registry of live service instances for client-side discovery
invariants: Must be reachable for Eureka clients to register and refresh their instance list
failureModes: If down, existing clients keep cached instance lists (short-term resilience) but new instances cannot register and stale instances are not evicted
testHints: Verify a dependent service still serves cached routes when this module is unreachable

nodes.summary: Owns the employee roster (including PII: name, phone, address, gender) in its own MongoDB collection; the only writer of employees, and the caller that stitches an employee's salary together by fetching department data from department-service over HTTP.
responsibilities: CRUD, search, and Excel bulk-upload for employees
Resilience wrapping (circuit breaker/retry/timeout) around that outbound call

crossCutting.topic: Missing authentication across every REST surface
crossCutting.text: No module in this workspace depends on spring-security or any other auth mechanism (confirmed by scanning every pom.xml for Maven dependencies). Every REST endpoint listed across department-service, employee-service, report-service, and sheduler-service is reachable by any caller who can route to it, exposing employee PII, department salary data, and write/upload operations without credentials. This is ISSUE-002's root cause and applies uniformly, not per-endpoint.

crossCutting.topic: Employee schema duplicated across three services with no shared library
crossCutting.text: employee-service, report-service, and sheduler-service each define their own `Employee` @Document entity and `GenderType`/`EmployeeType` enums with identical fields, rather than depending on a shared model module. A schema change in one (e.g. adding a field) will not propagate to the others, and each service's Mongo collection is populated/read independently, so there is no single source of truth enforced by the code for what an 'employee' looks like across services.

crossCutting.topic: Unbounded findAll() usage on the employees collection
crossCutting.text: sheduler-service (EmployeeSchedulerServiceImpl.getAllEmployees, backing both GET /api/v1/employee and the cron job) and report-service (EmployeeReportServiceImpl.getEmployees, backing GET /api/v1/export) both call the Spring Data findAll() inherited from MongoRepository with no Pageable or filter, reading the entire employees collection into memory on every invocation. This is ISSUE-001's root cause and scales linearly (or worse, for the report-service nested-loop join) with collection size.

crossCutting.topic: Cross-service HTTP responses dereferenced without null checks
crossCutting.text: Both employee-service (EmployeeServiceImpl.getEmployeeSalary) and report-service (EmployeeReportServiceImpl.getEmployees) call `.block()` on a WebClient response from department-service and immediately dereference the result (`.getDepartmentName()`, `Arrays.asList(departmentResponses)`) with no null check. department-service returning null, an empty body, or an error status will surface as an unhandled NullPointerException in both callers; only employee-service's salary route has a circuit breaker masking this at the controller layer.

crossCutting.topic: Deployment ordering dependency on configuaration-server and discovery-service
crossCutting.text: department-service, employee-service, report-service, and sheduler-service all depend on spring-cloud-starter-config and spring-cloud-starter-bootstrap, meaning they fetch their configuration from configuaration-server during the bootstrap phase before the main application context starts, and all register with discovery-service as Eureka clients. Neither dependency carries a Java call edge in the code graph, but both must be up before the other four services can start cleanly.
